More than 10,000 senior members of this terrorist organization will be banned from ever setting

The IRGC has been surging against the wand this year, up about 12% since January 1st.
That's helped our next guest, who has a big bet on a weaker wand.
Joining us right now is Crescent Capital founder, CIO, and CEO Kevin Smith.
Crescent Capital has $300 million in assets under management.
His global macro hedge fund up, we should say, 34% year-to-date in what has been a tough one.
Kevin, nice to see you.
Tell us about this bet and how long do you think you can keep it on for at this point?
Well, this is a trade we've had on for quite some time, actually.
It really started for us in 2015.
And we've been playing it in a kind of a Nassim Tlaib kind of a strategy with a put option,
looking for a black swan event.
And we haven't had that black swan yet, but we have had a pretty steady devaluation of the yuan over these last eight years.
And we've made money on it five out of the last eight years.
But we think the real big devaluation, the more serious crisis is still coming.
A serious crisis in China?
Well, a currency crisis.
Really, we think of it as a twin banking and currency crisis.
And if you look at the banking assets in China, they have grown sevenfold since the global financial crisis.
Sevenfold over the last 14 years.
And this is really something that's done.
We've never seen this before in any major country for any major currency anywhere on the planet.
So what if you're not buying this?
I mean, it sounds like you like gold, too, right?
We are we're big fans of precious metals at Crescat.
We have what we call the macro trade of the century right now.
And that is really being long inflation hedge assets.
Gold, of course, qualifies first and foremost, being short, long duration financial assets that are overvalued.
And then, you know, and then we want to be we want to be actually long the dollar.
We want to be short, you know, long duration assets.
We want to be long gold.
But we want to be long gold in the in the fiat currencies that are the most overvalued on the planet.
To us right now, that's, you know, that's China.
Thank you.
Thank you.

if it continues to give safe haven to people who are awaiting sanctions.
And this comes after the city said that it would not take any action

who is said to be very close to the Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The Nord is a $500 million luxury yacht owned by the Russian billionaire Alexei Mordechov.
The 142-metre-long super-yacht has two helipads, a cinema hall
and also more than a dozen luxury cabins.

and the United States has said that the transparency of Hong Kong's business environment

fleeing sanctions that have been imposed on Russia to the safe haven in the city.

depended on its adherence to international laws and standards.
For the first time, Apple has been asking its suppliers to move AirPods and Beats headphone
manufacturing to India.
The move comes after Apple is diversifying away from China to reduce supply chain disruptions
caused by its strict zero-COVID policy and tensions with the U.S.
Sources from Nikkei Asia said that the information comes from two of Apple suppliers and from Apple itself.
According to three sources familiar with the situation,
Apple has been discussing raising production in India as early as next year with suppliers.
The plan includes key acoustics devices.
Similarly, iPhone's largest assembler, Foxconn, also plans to manufacture Beats headphones in India.
It expects to produce AirPods there as well.
Luxshare Precision Industry and its affiliates, another Apple supplier,
aim to make AirPods in India too.
The company already makes AirPods for Apple in Vietnam and China.
More than 70 million AirPods are shipped annually, second only to the iPhone.
Its production shifted from China to Vietnam in 2019 amid the U.S.-China tariff war.
It was one of the first Apple items mass-produced outside of China.
In terms of Beats headphones, sources from Nikkei Asia said most Beats productions now stay in Vietnam.
AirPods and Beats manufacturing in India would expand Apple's production foothold there,
where the latest iPhone will be made, according to a recent announcement.
Notably, Apple began having older iPhone models produced in India by Wishtron in 2017,
but has boosted its manufacturing since last year.
In addition, Apple initially manufactured in India to serve the vast local market,
but is now growing the country as a strategic production center to serve markets like Europe.
China's bond market has been bleeding as the world's second-largest economy is slowing down rapidly,
pushing capital to other destinations.
Reuters cited the latest Institute of International Finance data, reporting that capital outflows from
China's bond market reached $1.4 billion in September.
Over the past eight months, China's debt markets evaporated a total of $98.2 billion,
mainly due to the economic slowdown.
International investors have lost confidence in China and pulled capital from this market due
to the COVID pandemic, the lockdowns and faltering housing market, and other issues which led to
the economic downturn.
The latest data pointed to further cooling of the economy, with China's industrial production
barely growing in September and the service sector slowing.
In addition, the economy is still struggling amid pandemic control measures and weaker global demand.
According to Mark Reed, head of fixed-income desk research at Mijuho Securities Asia,
there is another driver of the selldown in Chinese bonds.
